ai.subject: Anatomy
ai.summary: The phrenic nerve originates from C3‑C5, runs through the neck, thorax, and diaphragm, providing motor control and sensory input. It is crucial for breathing and can be injured in many clinical settings.

sections.p: The phrenic nerve is a mixed motor and sensory nerve that supplies the diaphragm, the main muscle of respiration. It carries motor fibers from C3‑C5 and sensory fibers from the diaphragm and pericardium.
It arises from the cervical plexus, descends along the anterior scalene muscle, pierces the thoracic cavity, and runs on the pericardium to the diaphragm.
It lies medial to the subclavian artery, anterior to the lung apex, and posterior to the brachial plexus. It is adjacent to the phrenic artery and veins.
The phrenic artery, a branch of the thoracic aorta or internal thoracic artery, supplies the nerve.
Motor fibers from C3‑C5, sensory fibers from diaphragm and pericardium, and sympathetic fibers.
It contracts the diaphragm during inspiration and provides sensory feedback for diaphragmatic pain and pericardial irritation.
Injury can cause diaphragmatic paralysis, leading to respiratory distress. Causes include trauma, surgery, infections, and inflammatory diseases.

sections.p: Remember the mnemonic "C3‑C5 keep the diaphragm alive" for origin. Referred pain to the shoulder (phrenic‑supraclavicular overlap) is a classic sign.

whenToSeekHelp: Severe dyspnea, sudden chest pain with shoulder referral, or inability to breathe after trauma or surgery

faq.q: What causes referred pain to the right shoulder?
faq.a: The phrenic nerve shares C3‑C5 segments with supraclavicular nerves, so diaphragmatic irritation refers pain to the shoulder.

faq.q: Can a low‑resource setting diagnose phrenic nerve palsy?
faq.a: Yes, a chest X‑ray showing an elevated hemidiaphragm and bedside ultrasound of diaphragmatic motion are practical tools.

faq.q: What is the most common cause of phrenic nerve injury?
faq.a: Surgical trauma during neck or thoracic procedures, especially central line placement or cardiac surgery.
